items.example: That show jumped the shark in season five.
items.exampleTr: O dizi beşinci sezonda sınırı aştı, saçmaladı.
items.simple: Something that was good gets silly and bad.
dialogue: A: Do you still watch it?
B: Honestly, it's about to jump the shark.
items.note: Friends ve HIMYM hayranlarının dizi eleştirilerinde.

items.example: His question came out of left field.
items.exampleTr: Sorusu hiç beklenmedik bir yerden geldi.
items.simple: Something surprising that no one thought about.
dialogue: A: Did you see that twist coming?
B: No, it had to come out of left field.
items.note: The Big Bang Theory ve Seinfeld'de.

items.example: He flew off the handle over a parking ticket.
items.exampleTr: Bir otopark cezası yüzünden tepesi attı.
items.simple: Get very angry very fast.
dialogue: A: Why is Dad yelling?
B: He'll fly off the handle over small things.
items.note: Malcolm in the Middle'da baba karakterinde.

items.example: Don't try to pull a fast one on me.
items.simple: Trick someone in a sneaky way.
dialogue: A: The price changed after I signed.
B: He tried to pull a fast one on you.

items.example: If you think I took it, you're barking up the wrong tree.
items.simple: You blame the wrong person or choose the wrong way.
dialogue: A: I know you stole my sandwich.
B: You always bark up the wrong tree, Sam.

items.tr: çaresizce umut aramak, saman çöpüne sarılmak
items.example: He's grasping at straws to save the deal.
items.simple: Try any weak idea when you are in a bad spot.
dialogue: A: He says maybe it's a mistake.
B: He'll grasp at straws until the end.

items.example: The letter was a red herring, not a real clue.
items.exampleTr: Mektup gerçek ipucu değil, yanıltıcı bir şeydi.
items.simple: Something that sends you the wrong way.
dialogue: A: So the man in the hat did it?
B: No, he was a red herring.

items.en: get a taste of your own medicine
items.example: Now he'll get a taste of his own medicine.
items.simple: Feel the bad thing you did to others.
dialogue: A: Dave pranked me back!
B: About time you get a taste of your own medicine.
items.note: Malcolm in the Middle'da kardeş intikamlarında.

items.example: Don't rub salt in the wound, I already feel awful.
items.simple: Make a sad person feel worse.
dialogue: A: I told her you lost the bet.
B: Please don't rub salt in the wound.

items.example: They lost my bag and, to add insult to injury, the hotel was full.
items.exampleTr: Çantamı kaybettiler, üstüne otel de doluydu.
items.simple: Something bad happens, then something worse too.
dialogue: A: The car broke down, and then it rained.
B: Add insult to injury: I had no umbrella.

items.example: Our whole plan is hanging by a thread.
items.simple: Something could stop or fall very easily.
dialogue: A: Is the deal still on?
B: Barely. It could hang by a thread for days.

items.example: Let's cut to the chase. How much do you want?
items.simple: Skip the extra talk and say the main thing.
dialogue: A: Before we begin, let me tell you about my day.
B: Let's cut to the chase, please.

items.example: Organising this family dinner is like herding cats.
items.exampleTr: Bu aile yemeğini organize etmek kedi gütmek gibi.
items.simple: A job that is very hard because nobody listens.
dialogue: A: How's the wedding planning?
B: It's like herding cats.

items.en: the pot calling the kettle black
items.example: You calling me messy? That's the pot calling the kettle black.
items.exampleTr: Bana dağınık mı diyorsun? Kendi kusurunu görmüyorsun.
items.simple: You blame someone for a fault you also have.
dialogue: A: You never clean up!
B: That's the pot calling the kettle black.

items.en: kick the can down the road
items.example: We keep kicking the can down the road on this.
items.simple: Wait to fix a problem instead of fixing it now.
dialogue: A: Are we choosing a date?
B: No, we'll just kick the can down the road.

items.en: wouldn't touch it with a ten-foot pole
items.example: That deal? I wouldn't touch it with a ten-foot pole.
items.exampleTr: O anlaşma mı? Yanına bile yanaşmam.
items.simple: You want to stay far away from something bad.
dialogue: A: Want to buy his old van?
B: I wouldn't touch it with a ten-foot pole.

items.example: Their big plan went down in flames.
items.exampleTr: Büyük planları büyük bir fiyaskoyla bitti.
items.simple: Fail in a very big, loud way.
dialogue: A: How will the date go?
B: I'm afraid it will go down in flames.
items.note: The Office ve Seinfeld'de fiyasko anlatımında.

items.en: burn the candle at both ends
items.example: He's burning the candle at both ends this month.
items.exampleTr: Bu ay kendini yıpratana kadar çalışıyor.
items.simple: Do too much and sleep too little.
dialogue: A: You look so tired.
B: Don't burn the candle at both ends, Sam.
items.note: The Big Bang Theory'de bilim insanlarının çalışma temposunda.

items.en: go back to the drawing board
items.example: The test failed, so it's back to the drawing board.
items.simple: Start again with new ideas after failing.
dialogue: A: The client hated our idea.
B: Then we go back to the drawing board.
items.note: The Big Bang Theory ve The Office'te.

items.example: I have a bone to pick with you about last night.
items.exampleTr: Dün gece yüzünden seninle konuşacaklarım var.
items.simple: You are upset with someone and want to talk about it.
dialogue: A: Why is Mom so cold today?
B: I have a bone to pick with her, that's why.

items.en: the writing is on the wall
items.example: The writing is on the wall for this company.
items.simple: You can already see something will end badly.
dialogue: A: Will they close the branch?
B: The writing is on the wall.

items.example: This show loves to push the envelope.
items.simple: Try something new that goes past the usual limit.
dialogue: A: Why try such a wild idea?
B: I like to push the envelope.
items.note: The Big Bang Theory'de bilim ve Brooklyn Nine-Nine'da.

items.example: You broke it, so now face the music.
items.simple: Take the punishment for what you did.
dialogue: A: Dad's home and he saw the car.
B: Time to face the music.
items.note: Malcolm in the Middle'da ceza anlarında.
